articleTitle: Review on Power Quality Issues in EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are playing a crucial role in achieving the carbon neutral goal. To make the charging experience comparable with the refueling of the gasoline cars, more and more chargers are installed and connected to the grid. Meanwhile, the charging power is going up. As a result, more and more power quality issues associated with EV charging events have already been reported. In this paper, the power quality issues that are relevant to EV charging, including flicker, harmonics, and supraharmonics, are summarized. Their generation mechanisms, harm to the grid, and the promising mitigation measures are discussed. Case studies are also done to mimic the power quality issues in EV charging, and verify the analysis.

articleTitle: A Battery Digital Twin Based on Neural Network for Testing SoC/SoH Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Lithium ion cells are the preferred solution for the growing world of mobile applications. To avoid working conditions that can accelerate irreversible degradation reactions, two parameters must always be known, namely State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH). Since SoC and SoH cannot be measured directly with sensors on cells, they must be derived from the observation of voltage and current at the accessible connections. The literature on algorithms for SoC-SoH estimation is very rich and new advanced ones are continuously developed. However, the testing of algorithms on real batteries is very time consuming due to the need of many charge-discharge cycles in order to observe aging effects. These operations can take months in the lab. In this paper we present a Battery Digital Twin (BDT) that outputs a realistic voltage signal as a function of SoC and SoH inputs. The voltage signals produced by the BDT can later be used to feed SoC/SoH estimation algorithms. The BDT is thus a simulator for fast testing of battery parameter estimation algorithms. This paper presents a BDT developed in the Matlab-Simulink-Simscape environment. The non-linear Open Circuit Voltage (OCV) generator as a function of SoC/SoH is based on a feed forward Neural Network (NN) trained with real data from a publicly available repository. The internal complex impedance can assume fixed circuit configurations derived from typical Nyquist plots or can be dynamically adjusted by other trained NN as non-linear function of SoC/SoH.

articleTitle: Conceptual Modelling of an EV-Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology has contributed to the development process of many applications, including electric vehicles (EVs). The DT concept is to create a digital representation of a real physical asset and support its performance by utilizing simulation and optimization tools fed with real-time data. DT technology can be used to solve general problems related to EV motors, such as estimation of the driving torque and the internal rotor temperature. This paper provides the concepts for implementing a DT of an EV permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) based on its analytical performance model. DT architecture comprises two main components: virtual model and real-time data exchange set. The motor physical model (test bench) was provided in detail. An analytical performance q-d mathematical model supported by the motor equivalent circuit was explained. The motor virtual model was built based on the proposed analytical model using MATLAB/Simulink. Robot operating system V.2 (ROS2) node, implemented on a microcontroller, was used for real-time data exchange between the physical and the virtual motor models. The main target is to monitor the physical motor performance and estimate its torque through its digital twin. The obtained results from the DT showed the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis on a Single-Phase Inverter With a Reduced Component Count Power Decoupling Circuit
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: An experimental and simulation analysis of an active power decoupling method that does not require additional power semiconductors is presented in this paper. The inverter performance is analyzed in terms of capacitors requirement, efficiency, and steady-state operation and compared to the conventional inverter. The control method of the power decoupling method uses DC-link voltage to generate compensation voltage for controlling the voltage between the two inverter arms. In this way the low-frequency DC-link current ripple is attenuated to a negligible value, allowing the replacement of DC-link electrolytic capacitors with smaller and more reliable thin film capacitors. The design was also analyzed from the perspective of capacitors volume. A losses analysis was carried out on a 1kW rated inverter implemented with silicon carbide MOSFETs, which showed the performance of the proposed inverter and revealed further optimizations to be addressed.

articleTitle: Finite control set model predictive current control for reluctance synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a finite control set model predictive current control FCS-MPC for reluctance synchronous motor (RSM). Non-linear characteristics of d-q inductances have been applied to obtain an accurate model of the machine. These were used to calculate the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) strategy, and to predict the current space vector components for the control algorithm. The proposed control scheme has been implemented in Matlab/Simulink environment supported by the PLECS toolbox. An optimal prediction horizon was selected taking into account the minimization of the motor's torque ripples. Extensive simulation studies indicate high-performance operation of the RSM and torque ripple reduction. Experimental tests are also included.

articleTitle: Minimum Copper Losses Per Torque Optimization on Electrically Excited Synchronous Motors for Electric Vehicles Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Increased environmental and energy security concerns have made electric vehicles an attractive solution over the recent years. Therefore, improving their traction chain global efficiency, especially in high-speed region, became a major task in today's research. This paper investigates a novel optimization method applied on electric vehicles motorized by an Electrically Excited Synchronous Motor (EESM). The study proposes an algebraic method based on the Lagrange multiplier technique to control the motor torque efficiently while extending its speed limit using the additional degree of freedom offered by this type of machines. The reference currents are calculated offline and stored in lookup tables (LUT) using MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed method is compared to conventional Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) strategies applied on Internal Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (IPMSM) by maintaining the EESM excitation current constant and controlling the d-q axis currents for a likewise behavior. The optimization and speed limit extension benefits of the novel control scheme, especially in high-speed region, are emphasized via simulation results in the torque/speed domain.

articleTitle: Educational Platform for Remote Power Electronics Laboratory Classes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper concerns digital educational platform that can help students to remotely conduct measurements of basic power electronics converters. Remotely connected users can view real-time oscilloscope waveforms, register operation parameters such as voltages and currents, change operation point (e.g., duty cycle, frequency).

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Simulation and Economic Benefit Analysis for a Light Duty Urban Commercial Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Electrification of the conventional propulsion system revolution has been taking place in the automotive industry to seek a cleaner and safer transportation network across cities. The electrified powertrain has significantly reduced fossil fuel dependence and improved fuel economy. Moreover, optimal energy consumption as a trade-off between the conflicting demand to prolong driving mileage and the need for the vehicle to operate within the limit of the battery capacity is quite critical. This paper simulates the energy consumption per 1 kilometer and 100 kilometers of the distance covered by a VW Crafter with a 2.0 CR DTI Diesel Engine Vehicle. The traditional Combustion Engine (CI) system as a front-wheel-drive was replaced by a comparative study between a complex and simplified electrified drivetrain-based a 4-pole, Y-connected Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Motor (PMBLDCM) propulsion system. The energy consumed using the New European Drive Cycle (NEDC) test procedure was 0.15 kWh/km and 10.53 kWh/100km, respectively. Furthermore, this research proposes a Proportional Integral (PI) baseline control algorithm to regulate Motor and vehicle speeds. In this manner, the execution of the PI controller was confirmed by implementing a PID Control scheme. However, the performance of the traditional controls is not realistic and, therefore, not reliable due to the nonlinear nature of the system. Accordingly, performance integral criteria such as “Integral Square Error (ISE),” “Integral Absolute Error (IAE)” etc., were used to ascertain the optimal gains of the proposed control techniques.

articleTitle: Efficient Method of Identifying a Li-Ion Battery Model for an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for identifying the equivalent circuit model of a Li-Ion battery is described. The considered model consists of a non-linear state-of-charge - open-circuit voltage (SoC-OCV) and a second-order RC network. The parameters of the RC network are considered SoC-dependent. The proposed method requires only a single charging/discharging cycle for parameter identification and does not require either slow cycling or long battery resting periods in order to determine the SoC-OCV curve. Data analysis relies on a linear least-squares approach, with separate procedures for identifying the RC network parameters and the SoC-OCV curve. The identified model was verified on a dataset corresponding to a sports vehicle drive cycle, showing very good accuracy. Various approximations (e.g. polynomial, exponential, piecewise-affine) of the SoC-OCV curves were tested, yielding good accuracy for exponential and higher-order polynomial and piecewise-affine approximations.

articleTitle: A Comparison of DPWM and Inverter Loss Energy Based FCS-MPC for IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of a discontinuous pulse width modulation (DPWM) and a finite control set-model predictive control (FCS-MPC) when a power factor is lower than 0.866. An inverter loss energy-based algorithm, which has an objective to reduce inverter losses, is used in the FCS-MPC. Two control methods are implemented in an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) based drive system. The simulation results lead to the conclusion that the FCS-MPC can achieve a better current total harmonic distortion (THDi) and a better inverter efficiency than the DPWM does when the power factor is lower than 0.866.

articleTitle: Impact of the Various Components Consideration on Choosing Optimal Redundancy Strategy in MMC
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Power electronics converters will play a crucial role in power grid expansion. Superior advantages offered by MMC make it the most popular candidate amongst various converter topologies. However, due to a large number of components installed within MMC, reliability analysis is an unavoidable task that needs to be carried out to maximize the MMC's availability and positively affect the overall performance of the power system. To this end, applying redundancy at the converter level is one of the solutions to increase the reliability of the MMC. In this paper, the reliability of the MMC is evaluated during its useful lifetime according to various applied redundancy strategies. At the same time, it is proposed that optimal-decision making in redundancy strategy depends on the failure rate of which components are considered. It will be presented that the superiority of the applied redundancy can vary.

articleTitle: Series-Resonant DC-DC Interface Converter for Battery Integration into DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper focuses on the galvanically isolated series-resonant dc-dc converter (SRC) operating at low values of the quality factor of the resonant tank. This topology is considered as a bidirectional step-up front-end dc-dc converter with buck-boost functionality for integration of battery energy storage in dc microgrids. The main aim of the study is to develop a universal dc-dc converter for the parallel connection of batteries to the dc microgrid. The paper presents a closed-loop control system of the SRC capable of regulating the current of a battery and softly changing the power flow direction. The developed closed-loop control system is based on droop control for parallel operation in the dc microgrid. Experimental results show the performance of the developed converter in operation as a battery front-end interface converter in the dc microgrid. Depending on the voltage in the dc microgrid, the control system regulates the current of a battery and changes the power flow direction for storing energy in the battery or supplying the dc microgrid.

articleTitle: Current-Fed Dual Inductor Push-Pull Partial Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Conventional full power dc-dc converters are processing the whole power flowing from the source to the load, which critically limits the overall efficiency of the system. Coming to the fact that the converter can perform the required functions by processing only the mandatory fraction of power, which is called power processing. In this paper, a Series Partial Power Converter (S-PPC) based on the current-fed push-pull dc-dc converter is presented. In order to get the full benefit of the S-PPC, the converter should process power less than 25% of the overall system power. Current-fed push-pull converter modulation is designed to ensure that all switches are operating at soft-switching. Basic system analysis and system simulation are discussed in the paper

articleTitle: Comparison of square-wave and sinusoidal signal injection in sensorless polarity detection for PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper compares the non-modulated square-wave voltage injection-based and sinusoidal voltage injection-based polarity detection methods applicable in sensorless PMSM drives. A quadratic PMSM model extension is presented that serves as a basis for the polarity detection techniques. The comparison includes the polarity-dependent current components produced by the injected signals, the design parameters related to the injected signal features and their effect on the probability of correct polarity detection. The performance differences and possible application areas are also discussed.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of on-Street EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The uncoordinated charging of Electric Vehicles (EVs) into the grid increases the stochastic rebound peak on the grid. These charging demands can strain grid equipment at the street charging points in an area. In this study, a smart coordination approach is proposed for charging process management by considering the parking times of EVs. EV types with different characteristics are used in the smart coordination approach. This approach limits the charging powers to the minimum value between the charging point and the EV maximum power ratio. Also, the approach using quadratic programming (QP) for charge scheduling of 20 EV minimizes the cost of daily charging via the Generic Algebraic Modeling System (GAMS). The results show that EV charges occur within the maximum allowable grid limits, reducing the cost of charging. Additionally, the proposed smart coordination prevented the occurrence of daily on-grid rebound peaks at street charging points in the area.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Aortic Valve Detection and State Classification on Echocardiographies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Accurate assessment of the severity of aortic stenosis is essential for optimal therapeutic decision making. Echocardiography is the main imaging method used to assess the aortic valve (AV) and the severity of the aortic stenosis. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based method to detect the AV and to classify its state in parasternal long axis echocardiographic images. We rely on the Faster R-CNN algorithm for the AV detection and consider various architectures of VGG and Resnet as backbone. For the AV state classification, the AV features obtained for each frame are concatenated, and subsequently processed by a temporal model that outputs the prediction for each frame. The proposed model detects the aortic valve with a precision of 93.3% and with a recall close to 100%. The AV state classification achieves an accuracy of 94.4%. The proposed approach can be extended into a feature extractor for an aortic stenosis assessment application or can be used for pretraining the aortic stenosis classification.

articleTitle: Comparison and Simulation of Two Loss Minimization Algorithms for Field-oriented Control of Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison of two loss minimization algorithms for induction motor drives derived for the Gamma network and the inverse Gamma network is performed. The basic principle of the algorithm is to find the optimal flux at which the motor has the lowest power losses at the desired torque and speed. The optimal flux is then given as the desired flux to the flux controller in the d-axis. To validate the algorithms, motor models in a stationary frame were first built with non-constant magnetizing inductance and estimation of iron losses and mechanical losses. The proposed algorithms were verified by simulation in Matlab/Simulink environment with real motor parameters. The simulation results confirmed that both algorithms achieve the same efficiency. In terms of derivation complexity, the inverse Gamma network-derived model is simpler.

articleTitle: Estimating Inductances of Coils with Ferromagnetic Cores with a Data Acquisition System in a Noisy Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with the experimental setup, methodology and original algorithms used for the estimation of inductance specific to coils with ferromagnetic cores during the transient process associated to the discharging of a capacitor in a series RLC circuit. A data acquisition system characterized by a sampling rate of 100 kHz for each of the employed channels (one for current and one for voltage) and a resolution of analog to digital conversion of 12 bits is used. Experimental data were acquired on a test stand in an industrial environment where significant electromagnetic noise pollutes the acquired signals. An original program was conceived for the preprocessing of acquired data. It performs the removing of fake spikes and eliminates the electromagnetic noise, computes the signal to noise ratios and allows the user to select variable coordinates for zooms by using the graphical interface in order to provide accurate estimations of the inductance in different moments. Two case studies are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Designing High Power Density Induction Motors for Electric Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Designing high-power-density electric motors for propulsion has become an increasingly important issue in the past few decades. This is not only because electric vehicles are projected to become the main private transportation means in near future, but also because of the ever so important metro and railway transport requirements. Along with these application areas, electric aircraft propulsion is also coming into focus in recent years. Electric motors for traction are required to have high torque density, high efficiency over a wide speed range and are required to be robust. In recent years, permanent magnet (PM) motors became the favorite choice for such applications because of their higher efficiency than other types of motors. Increasing demand for permanent magnets is likely to cause supply problems. Therefore, permanent magnet-free alternative motor types are of much interest. In this paper, the authors present the design of a 125 kW induction motor for railway application. This design has 3-times the power density of a commercial induction motor. The designed motor is manufactured and its test results are used for establishing an accurate finite-element model for the prediction of its performance. This model is used to investigate the effect of magnetic loading choice, slot shape and magnetic material choice on the efficiency of the motor. It is shown that with the same basic dimensions the efficiency of the motor can be increased to 96% which is comparable with a similar size PM motor.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Verification of Planar Transformer for Multiport Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper describes the design and verification of a planar transformer with windings integrated into a printed circuit board (PCB). The planar transformer represents the main element for power transmission in a multiport power converter with three ports. The ANSYS software was used for the verification of the proposed planar transformer. Designed transformers were used as a coupling between ports of the multiport power converter.

articleTitle: Improved Efficiency and Power Density in EV Inverter Design Using a Novel SiC Power Module with Enanched Direct-cooled Inverter (EDI)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents how the Marelli in-house designed and built, ultra-compact SiC (Silicon Carbide) Power Module with direct cooled substrate can contribute to the realization of an inverter with outstanding power density and efficiency. After presenting the unique characteristics of SiC devices when compared to standard Si when it comes to high-current, high-efficient applications, we will then address the challenges of building and producing a compact, high-current capable power module using direct substrate cooling. Finally, we will present the design and validation results for the implementation of an inverter built with this technology and driving a high-speed motor.

articleTitle: Optimization of Injected Voltage Amplitude for Low-Speed Sensorless Control of PMSM with High-Frequency Pulse Signal Injection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) in low-speed operation is a challenging task. High-frequency (HF) signal injection methods have been successfully applied for low-speed sensorless control of PMSM. One of the most recent methods is the HF pulse signal injection method in which a series of HF voltage pulses are injected into the d-axis voltage reference. A control period of the sensorless algorithm is segmented into subperiods for injection and subperiod for an update of the field-oriented algorithm. This approach brings new possibilities and research questions as what should be the optimal amplitude value of the injected voltage. In this paper, a design and verification of the optimization procedure by calculating root-mean-square error values of the selected estimated values are presented. The optimal value of the injected voltage amplitude has been found for the given operating point by using MATLAB/Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: Axially-Laminated-Anisotropic-rotor Reluctance Synchronous Motor characterization: analytical design, key FEM validations and preliminary experiments: 10kW, 2.4-4.8krpm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a realistic preliminary design of an 4 pole reluctance synchronous machine with axially laminated anisotropic rotor. Key FEM validation performance for 10kW, 2400-4800rpm and a few stand still ac and dc tests on the prototype suggest the proposed solution is a promising one for competitive traction applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Permanent Magnet Electric Motors Used in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Lately, PM (permanent magnet) motors have started to be used frequently due to advantages such as high efficiency, high power density, high torque, lower losses, lower magnet costs, and more effective control with the development of power electronics. PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor) types and BLDCM (brushless direct current motor) types, two members of PM motors, have become frequently used motors in electric vehicles (EVs). In this study, PMSM and BLDCM are compared by optimizing magnet thicknesses, structures, and stator winding turn numbers, to improve the efficiency, using ANSYS Maxwell and ANSYS RMxprt software. In the study, surface mount magnet synchronous motor SPMSM with the inner rotor, V-shaped PM inner rotor IPMSM (interior permanent magnet synchronous motor), BLDCM with inner rotor embedded channel mount magnet, BLDCM with inner rotor embedded magnet, BLDCM with inner rotor surface mount magnet and BLDCM with outer rotor are compared.

articleTitle: Design of IoT based flood monitoring and alerting system
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is the development of an automatic flood detection and prevention system, mainly oriented for residential use, but with possibility to be used in industrial applications as well. According to a study conducted by a German company regarding water damage occurrence and floods in EU households, the participants believed that water damage occurs in only 37% of households. Over 57% of European households suffer from water damage. Different causes can lead to floods and unavoidable water damage. The study participants considered that there are three main causes which may lead to floods: bursting pipes, small cracks due to corrosion, material fatigue or due to frost and defective laundry machines or dishwashers. The occurring ratio for each type of incident has been established as well. The first position is being taken by bursting pipes, the most common incident, responsible for over 48% of the total residential flood incidents. The risk for this type of incident to occur is 21%. Defects caused by corrosion or frost take the second position in the ranking, with a total of 28% of total incidents and the occurring rate is 19%. The last place is being taken by defects caused by small pipe cracks due to material fatigue, the chances for this kind of defect to occur rise to 19% of total. This paper aims to develop an automatic flood detection and prevention system, especially in the residential environment. The aim is to obtain an economical and effective alternative to the technical solutions available on the market. A wireless solution that is not dependent of a connection or a central control unit will be developed.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Soft-Switching DC-DC Converter with Simple Secondary Turn-Off Snubber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper describes the analysis, simulation, and measurement results of a high-frequency soft-switching dc-dc converter with a simple secondary Turn-off snubber. The converter utilizes a full-bridge topology with pulse-width modulation and a half-wave rectifier with one secondary side transistor. The control algorithm completely removes circulating current and ensures zero-voltage and zero-current switching of the primary-side transistor for the full load range. The secondary side turn-off snubber ensures zero-voltage turn-off for the secondary-side transistor. The principle of operation is verified by measurements on a 2 kW, 100 kHz laboratory model of the proposed dc-dc converter.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Reliability Assessment of Buck Quasi-Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores reliability assessment of various Quasi-Resonant (QR) buck DC-DC converters including zero current/voltage switching and half-wave/full-wave topologies. The impacts of output power, input voltage, output voltage, and time duration on the failure rate of each component are investigated, then overall reliability performance of each converter is evaluated. A detailed comparison is performed in which reliability metric of buck soft switching topologies is compared with each other as well as their parent hard switching topology. Eventually, mean time to failure of the converters is analyzed. This approach provides insightful information for selecting the topology or components for the purpose of designing QR converters. To achieve the reliability of these converters, first, the required equations to evaluate the effective factors on the reliability are obtained. Then reliability metric values are calculated for three cases in each of which a key parameter of the converters varies over a specified range.

articleTitle: Wireless capacitive energy transfer system – preliminary results
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a capacitive wireless power transfer system. System description, simulation model and laboratory test bench have been presented. Preliminary simulation and laboratory results have been presented. The directions of further work were defined. The work was carried out under the HEET II (High Efficiency Energy Transfer) project, financed by the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS).

articleTitle: Modeling a Time Domain Reflectometer using Matlab/Simulink for detection of faults in electrical cables
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a modeling method based on time domain reflectometry for detection faults in electrical cables using Matlab/Simulink. The paper has four sections. The importance of electrical cables in electrical distribution system is highlighted in the introduction section. The second section contains the basic principles of the time domain reflectometry which are used to create the presented model from the fourth section. The last part emphasizes the usefulness of the proposed method and the possibilities for its further development.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of Global Parameters of Induction Machine for Fault Prediction in Rotor Bars
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Electrical machines play an essential role in numerous industrial applications. Modern energy systems, including wind turbines or electric vehicles, are prone to damage and failures. In those devices, unexpected failures often mean economic loss, environmental problems, and danger to human life in the worst case. For developing a system that is able to predict potential faults, it is important to understand what data is to be used for training. In this paper, a preliminary analysis of global electrical parameters was conducted. For comparison, different control environments, loads, and damage progressing stages were considered.

articleTitle: Robust Estimation of the State Variables of Two-Mass System using Multilayer Observer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In the paper the issues related to the application of the Multi-Layer Observer (MLO) for a drive system with elastic joint in the case of parameter mismatch are presented. After an introduction where the topic of estimation in the field of drive systems with an elastic joint is briefly presented, the main point of the paper is described. Then the mathematical model of the drive with elasticity is demonstrated and control structure is shown. Then, the idea of the MLO is discussed. Simulation and experimental results showing the properties of the MLO working in closed-loop structure are included, accompanied by experimental results.

articleTitle: Tapped inductor Boost with exploitation of the stray energy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Tapped inductor DC-to-DC converters are interesting circuits, the winding ratio of the two windings mounted on the same core change the voltage transformation ratio compared to the untapped inductor. The tapped inductor converters are especially useful, when high or low voltage transformation ratios have to be realized. The disadvantage of this concept is that the coupling between the two windings is not total and can be described by the stray or leakage inductance. This stray inductance leads to a high overvoltage at the active switch, and therefore also across other elements of the converter. After a short summery of the ideal tapped Boost converter, the design of an RCD snubber which limits the overvoltage is explained. To improve the efficiency of the converter two active snubber networks are treated, which feed the energy stored in the snubber capacitor into the input source or into the output circuit. Simulations are used to prove these considerations.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Weak Grid Totem-Pole PFC Based on Stroboscopic Mapping
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Wind farms are in remote areas, and most wind power is under weak network condition after long-distance transmission, so it can no longer be regarded as an ideal power source. Stroboscopic mapping is a discrete mathematical model for analyzing nonlinear dynamic behavior and operation stability of power electronic converters. Aiming at the different working states of totem-pole PFC under weak power supply condition, a stroboscopic mapping mathematical model is established, and a modulation mode with variable frequency carrier amplitude is proposed to compensate the nonlinear behavior of zero-crossing distortion of input current. Then, the folded diagrams of totem-pole PFC input current and pre-bridge input voltage after compensation are drawn. The operation state of the converter is discussed based on the discrete model and folded diagrams. Simulation results verify the validity of the compensation method. By comparing the waveforms in time domain with the folded diagrams of the same parameters, the correctness of using folded diagram to analyze the stability of converter is verified.

articleTitle: Design of Two-Channel LED Stand-Alone Solar Lamp Driver Prototype for Biodynamic Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with design of LED driver as a part of an efficient solar-powered streetlamp based on biodynamic lighting. The contribution of this paper is experimental verification of the designed solution in form of a fully functional battery powered SSLS prototype.

articleTitle: Cooling channel optimization in power inverter design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to develop and optimize a proper cooling channel for a power module used in high-power three-phase inverters for electrified vehicles. Specifically, the cooling plate and the channel are designed by using steady-state 3D-computational-fluid-dynamic (CFD) tool. Subsequently, an optimization tool with dedicated algorithms is used to define the optimal layout, pin-fins and channel's geometry in terms of inlet vs outlet pressure drop and power chip's thermal performances. The simulations were performed using OptiSlang tool provided by Ansys.

articleTitle: Project Based Learning to Approach the Topic of Efficient Energy Conversion By Integrating Responsive Building Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to promote, in an educational content, the aspects of an efficient building design requirements, based on efficient energy conversion concept and by using an integrative designing approach. The main objective of the research is to propose a learning scenario regarding an actual and global real-life problem: the energy saving. The study intends to achieve a phenomenological approach of the topic, in a transdisciplinary manner. Regarding the educational goals, the research proposes the Project Based Learning (PBL) strategy to develop analysis and solutions for different learning objectives defined on the subject. The finality of the paper is a model of thinking a real-life problem through a collaborative work, integrating designing and know how transfer. This model could be use by students, by project teams or in a long-life learning approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effect of Increasing Motor Voltage from 690-V to 1000-V on 1.5-MW Motor Drive Design for Large-Scale Electric Propulsion Ship
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: For large-scale electric propulsion ship, line voltage of independent microgrid in the ship can be increased from 690-V to 1000-V to reduce filter weight of grid-side systems. This paper investigates the advantages and disadvantages in terms of 1.5-MW motor drive design when the rated motor voltage is increased from 690-V to 1000-V. The analysis is performed in the order of induction motor, DC-link capacitor, and switching device for motor drive. The simulation results from MATLAB/SIMULINK are expressed by map considering various motor operating conditions. For fair comparison, the cost analysis is also conducted. As a result, this study finds that the motor drive loss and switch junction temperature are reduced, but the motor drive efficiency is also decreased at low-speed and low-torque operating condition. Therefore, we conclude that there is the need for research about improvement of motor drive efficiency at this operating condition.

articleTitle: Concept of Solar Street Lighting with Hexagonal Solar Panels
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison of flat and hexagonal solar panels is provided. Furthermore, charging using MPPT algorithm is described and its properties in basic tests are analyzed. The end of the paper deals with the description of the designed solution of the street lighting concept in detail. The designed solution is experimentally tested using a form of a fully functional battery powered SSLS prototype.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Isolated dc-dc Converters for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Isolated dc-dc converters are particularly important for utilizing renewable energy. These converters are used for direct connection to the dc microgrid or as voltage boosters for on/off-grid ac applications. This article examines and evaluates five popular types of isolated dc-dc converters for low-power applications. In this study, by examining the performance of converters, the general equations governing these converters have been extracted. The converter components are then designed for a low-power application. Using simulations in Simulink/MATLAB, these converters have been evaluated and compared from different perspectives.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Model Development for a Continuous Dynamic Black-Box System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper describes a method of a black-box fuzzy model design based only on the system measured input/output quantity without necessity of any preliminary knowledge about the modeled system order and without any access to system state variables. The method is based on the use of continuous linear dynamic filters of the first order, which in practice are easily feasible and are always stable. The proposed methodology is applied in the fuzzy model design for a three-phase induction motor which represents a higher order nonlinear system. Simulation measurements in MATLAB confirmed the accuracy, effectiveness and good dynamic properties of the proposed fuzzy model and also its applicability to continuous dynamic systems with as little previous knowledge as possible. The aim of the article is to show that the automated fuzzy modeling techniques can be used also to obtain an accurate fuzzy model of a low complexity based on a set of series of measurements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Unbalanced Dual Induction Motor Drive Configuration Supplied by Single Inverter for Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Parallel supply of two induction motors by a single inverter is nowadays a mature technology that has several industrial applications, such as railway. Under ideally symmetrical FOC at equal mechanical speed, both motors draw the same current and produce the same torque and flux. However, parameter deviations, in particular stator resistance, can arise due to several factors, such as temperature variations or inappropriate cable contacts. This leads to a complex distribution of the current vectors, flux vectors and torque distribution between both motors, which strongly depends on the actual torque and speeds. In this work, the resulting asymmetrical flux and current sharing under non-identical dual motors will be analysed and further investigated for the purpose of parameter estimation. It will be proved that the stator current vector as well as the rotor flux vector, in both magnitude and angle, provide relevant information about the stator resistance in the proximity to zero speed operation. Simulations are presented to demonstrate the effect of stator resistance variations on current and flux sharing for non-equal parameter dual motors under average FOC. An experimental test bench with two unequal motors is presented. Experimental results prove the meaningful information that current vector and flux vector contain about the different stator resistance of the two machines.

articleTitle: Improvements to the VSM current controller for better grid performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Output current control is widely used as the innermost control loop of inverters, in particular virtual synchronous machines (VSM). The realization of this controller is commonly based on a PI controller working in a synchronous reference frame. The controller should mitigate the grid currents distortion and the unsteady amplitudes caused by A/D converter imperfections, measurement errors and processing delays. The elimination of any DC component in the output currents is another relevant demand. The literature indicates that the current controller parameters are usually chosen by experimental tuning. In this paper, we propose a fast current controller design procedure that provides compensation for the processing delays and eliminates the DC components of the grid-side currents. We propose to control also the zero component of the output currents (which helps in an unbalanced grid). We present the performance of the novel features of our current controller through a series of simulations, comparing it to the performance of the same controller without the proposed additional features. In addition, we compare our new current controller's design with one proposed in the literature. The results show that the new current controller leads to a better performance of the VSM in terms of output active power oscillations and stability.

articleTitle: Predictive control of induction motor fed by LC filter and transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of control algorithm for induction motor drive with the transformer and input LC filter. Such drive configuration is often used for drive of submersible pumps or in the testing facilities, where the transformer enables to adapt the voltage range of tested drive. The complexity of the drive and its model makes it difficult to employ conventionally used FOC based control algorithms. In this paper we introduce the control algorithm combining the idea of FOC with the predictive control. An important contribution of this paper is the mathematical model design enabling reconstruction of particular control variables necessary for proper control implementation. PI controllers are used to design the stator current references and simple predictive controller is used to secure the stator current tracking. Resulting control structure is very simple and requires very little tuning. The simulations were carried out to test designed control algorithm.

articleTitle: High performance small ALA-rotor reluctance synchronous motor: preliminary design for variable speed with key FEM validation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Due to its higher magnetic saliency axially-laminated anisotropic (ALA) –rotor reluctance synchronous machines are credited with higher torque density, efficiency×power factor but, due to “the prejudice” of „hard to fabricate” and low rotor q axis low harmonics losses, it was studied less in recent years. This paper introduces a shaft-less (non-through shaft) two pole rotor configuration with slits which is deemed to ease the fabrication and reduce rotor q-axis flux harmonics losses, and then, for a rated power of 450W at 3000 rpm, develops a rather complete preliminary (analytical) design forecasting superior performance in terms of torque density and efficiency×power factor for variable speed. This performance is then checked/validated by key FEM investigations (on torque production, inductances, efficiency and power factor).

articleTitle: EV-Powertrain Test Bench for Digital Twin Development
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the development of a PC-controlled experimental bench dedicated to the testing of an electric vehicle (EV) powertrain. The test bench was built with the goal of facilitating the creation of digital twin (DT) that simulate the real EV propulsion drive system. Different components of the test bench were described in detail. The potentialities of the developed bench are highlighted through the emulation of different automotive cycles including acceleration and braking.

articleTitle: Fixed-Frequency Sliding Mode Control in Synchronous Reference Frame for Three-Phase LCL Filtered Active Front-End Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this study, a two-level voltage source converter based active front end (AFE) is designed. An LCL filter is used to suppress input current harmonics. A fixed switching frequency sliding mode controller is designed in synchronous reference frame to control the grid currents. In addition to the grid current, a capacitor voltage loop is used to suppress the LCL filter resonance. A PI controller is employed to regulate the output DC voltage. In addition, another PI controller is employed to generate the capacitor voltage reference, thus, requirement of the filter components is eliminated, and robust control structure is achieved. The performance of the proposed controller is validated with MATLAB/Simulink simulations and also compared with conventional PI control in synchronous reference frame which employs a passive damping for LCL filter. The simulation results show that the proposed method draws sinusoidal currents with low harmonic content from the grid while it regulates the output voltage. Besides, it provides fast response and robust structure.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design and Comparison of 5 Phase and 6 Phase Fault Tolerant Outer Rotor Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines with Different Electrical Steel
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison of 5 phase and 6 phase fault tolerant outer rotor permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) with fractional slot concentrated winding (FSCW) is presented. The paper will show that machines with higher number of slots have less mass of active materials due to the decreased length of end windings. Further, if both conditions of outer rotor and fixed outer diameter apply, there exists only one optimal topology of FSCW from the point of view machine's torque/mass density. Finally, when comparing machines with cobalt iron (FeCo) and silicon iron (FeSi) electrical steel, the latter are cheaper, have lower iron losses and can be shorter than FeCo machines. However, when the main task is to reach high torque density per mass, FeCo machines are the better solution.

articleTitle: Simulation Method for Energy Estimation of Variable Speed Pump for Heating System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Model based energy management for a heating system driven by the circulating centrifugal pump with variable speed drive in household applications is a promising approach for potential energy savings. The paper presents a developed Matlab/Simulink model of an energy savings calculation for a dwelling supplied with a circulating heating system (HS). The heating system includes a circulating centrifugal pump that has a variable speed drive helping to carry out the control algorithm based on the energy management strategy. The model helps to select the proper control strategy to achieve the desired indoor climate by following the defined reference point to keep the indoor temperature within the desired range. It consists of several main parts such as parameters selection module, thermal module, and integrated circulating centrifugal pump. The proposed simulation model helps to determine the heating power that is necessary to satisfy thermal requirements for a residential building by taking into account the thermal criteria with minimal energy consumption. The model helps to evaluate the energy savings of the heating system in the broad range of outdoor temperature variations.

articleTitle: Experiments of SiC MOSFETs in high DC bus voltage Boost applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In high power DC-DC or AC-DC, there is a trend towards increasing the DC bus voltage. In this paper, two boost converter of 1300V DC bus are studied. In the circuit design, a new 2000V SiC MOSFET and a conventional serial-connected 1200V devices are used to achieve a 1300V DC bus requirement. The analytical calculations and experimental results show that the topology of 2000V devices can achieve higher efficiency and power density compared with topology of conventional serial-connected 1200V devices. The implementations of two topologies of boost converters are discussed and the advantages of 2000V SiC MOSFETs for high DC bus voltage applications are demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Current Sensor Fault-Tolerant Induction Motor Drive with Online Rotor Resistance Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this article, the current sensor (CS) fault-tolerant control (FTC) strategy for the induction motor (IM) drive has been presented. In CS postfault operation, missing phase currents are changing to currents estimated by the Virtual Current Sensor (VCS) algorithm, which is based on the DC-link voltage of voltage source inverter (VSI) and the rotor angular velocity. The paper presents the possibility of improving the accuracy of the stator current estimation using the method based on neural network (NN) for online estimation of the rotor resistance. The wide simulation tests for variable rotor and stator resistances in the IM model during sudden open-circuit fault of CS in phase <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{A}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}$</tex> show the high quality of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Turn-off Angle Analytical Calculation Method of a Passive Boost Converter with Parallel Type Capacitors for Switched Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This article proposes a boost converter and its analytical calculation method for switched reluctance motor (SRM) drives. In the proposed converter, each conventional asymmetric half-bridge driver for each phase has a passive front-end circuit. The front-end circuit consists of parallel type capacitors to store the energy and boost the phase voltages. With the boosted voltage, the SRM achieves lower torque ripple and lower coil energy recovery re percentage to the main power supply. An analytical method is used to calculate and analyze the motor drive for each phase. Optimization methods are used for controlling the proposed SRM drive to generate maximum torque. The motor, its drive and control are then simulated in a physical modeling simulation environment (MATLABISimscape™). The simulation results verified the analytical calculation method and confirmed the torque ripple improvement and reduction of coil magnetic energy re-flow to the source with the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Diagnosis Based on Wavelet Analysis and LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In order to realize online monitoring and improve the reliability of altitude simulation test equipment, wavelet analysis combining with neural network are proposed for fault diagnosis on sensors in an inlet pressure modulation system. Wavelet transform modulus maximum characteristic and high-frequency energy characteristic extraction obtains two-dimension wavelet decomposition level and type of the output signal from a pressure sensor. The extracted characteristic matrix by the two methods has the characteristics of sequence and is more distinct in discrimination for different signal than the characteristic vector. A LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural network is adopted to diagnose the fault of the sensor. The LSTM neural network prediction modulus is trained by using the sensor characteristic data set for different pressure conditions to improve its generalization ability. Testing and verification simulation show that, wavelet analysis combining the LSTM neural network prediction method can predict the random failures of a pressure sensor with satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: Phillips-Heffron model and damping torque analysis of synchronverter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Synchronverter is a virtual synchronous machine that completely reproduces the dynamic characteristics of synchronous generators. This paper derives the small signal model of synchronverter and build Phillips-Heffron Module of Synchron-verter (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PHMS$</tex>) based on the small signal model and natural frequency formula base on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PHMS$</tex>. Then, a virtual power system stabilizer (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$VPSS$</tex>) with speed deviation is designed based on natural frequency formula and damping torque analysis.

articleTitle: Controller Design of Dual Active Bridge Converter for Electric Vehicle Fast DC Charger Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The dual active bridge converter is mostly used in electric vehicle dc fast charger applications. Different types of modulation techniques can be used for dual active bridge converter control. In this paper, three modulation techniques i.e., single-phase shift modulation, triangular modulation, and trapezoidal modulation are presented. A comparison between single-phase shift modulation and triangular modulation is made and losses of both modulation techniques are analyzed to compare efficiencies. A controller for triangular modulation is designed and its performance is modeled and simulated via PLECS software. According to simulation results, the losses of the dual active bridge converter with triangular modulation are lower than half of the losses of the dual active bridge converter with single-phase shift modulation. The efficiency is increased from 95% to over 98% with triangular modulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Quaternion-based Method to Calculate Solar Irradiation on a Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The calculation of the solar irradiance is crucial in evaluating the performance of solar power plants and can ground their malfunction-analysis. In this paper, a new solar irradiance calculation method is presented to support these aims. The proposed method uses quaternions to describe the interaction between the Earth and the Sun regarding their motion to determine the angle of incidence of solar radiation on a given surface. The angular values obtained can be used to determine the estimated solar irradiance for a given surface using an arbitrary meteorological model. The method is highly scalable, thus the orientation and tilt of the surface can be varied by adding additional quaternion rotations. By changing the parameters and the meteorological model, it can be used to calculate the irradiance of a given surface of any object or device in the solar system. To show the accuracy of the proposed model, the generated data using the proposed method was compared with measured data from a meteorological station. The Pearson correlation coefficient showed a strong correlation (r=0.9613) between the measured and calculated data, confirming the proposed method's usefulness.

articleTitle: High Voltage High Frequency Single Wire Energy Transfer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a high voltage high frequency single wire energy transfer system for applications such as mining excavations. The Single Wire Energy Transfer system and its main electrical parameters are shown and described. The scope of the paper is limited to a study of the high frequency DC/AC/DC circuit of the SWET system. The feasibility of the proposed system was tested using a simulation model. Following the confirmation of feasibility by the means of simulation, a laboratory setup was prepared to test the system prototype. A good match was found between simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: Novel Driving Method for Brushless DC Motors Based on Higher Time-Harmonics in Input Voltages
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel driving method for brushless DC motors based on the direct injection of the higher time-harmonic components into the input voltages of the motor. The method aims to increase efficiency and reduce current and torque ripple, especially in applications where the motor operates most of the time with the load below its rating. The theoretical background of the method is described along with its mathematical description. The functionality of the method is validated by simulations and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Locked-rotor analysis of a Prius 2004 IPMSM motor with Digital-Twin-Distiller
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, an open-source tool, the Digital-Twin-Distiller, is used, which can encapsulate the realized FEM model into a web application as a digital twin. Many papers have proposed the cogging torque and the locked-rotor FEM calculations of the Toyota Prius 2004 motor. However, these models have minor differences, mainly in rotor topology. This paper presents a fully defined motor model and the effect of the flux barrier shape on the locked-rotor simulations. The results show that minor structural changes in the flux barrier's shape in the manufacturing tolerance range significantly affect the calculated torque.

articleTitle: Dynamic characteristic of swash-plate mechanism applied in quasi-free-piston generator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In order to avoid instability of free-piston engine (FPE) caused by removing power transmission mechanism, a novel quasi-free-piston engine (QFPE) which applies a swash-plate to constrain piston motion instead of transmitting mechanical power is proposed. Several permanent magnets are fixed to the linkages which are driven by the swash-plate. The working principle of quasi-free-piston was presented at first. Then the dynamic model of power transmission mechanism was established based on analysis of kinematic characteristics. After the gas force which was deprived from the thermodynamic model was applied on pistons, the electrical force acting on linkages were studied. As following a combining simulation model was established and analyzed. Results shows that acceleration of linkage of QFPE is much larger than traditional engine, which could improve the responding speed of QFPE to the instantaneous power demand. Benefiting from much shorter power transmission chain, higher efficiency could be achieved. However, the energy exchange between linkages and Z-shaft may lead to unnecessary power loss which needs further research in the future.

articleTitle: A Method for the Determination of Fault and Wear Types in Induction Motor's Bearings
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to investigate the feasibility of a method to determine the fault and wear type in induction motor's bearings. Instead of attaching a vibration sensor in close proximity to the bearings and examining its signal for any frequency components that indicate a flaw, this approach considers the stator current of the motor that is fed by a frequency inverter. Therefore, the motor (mounted on a test rig) will be quipped with bearings of known fault. By performing a thorough examination of the stator current signal, a method will be presented that is capable of indicating the fault and wear type of the bearing. In this work, the examined fault types (installed bearings with known fault) are fretting wear, abrasive wear and corroded bearings.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Techniques Based on M5P Indirect Control of Doubly Fed Induction Generator for Wind Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This study introduces M5P a control method to excerpt maximum capacity by wind power. Two methods of Utmost potency point tracking, is examined in detailed (with or without speed control). A regression model tree algorithm based on M5P fuzzy logic has been inserted into indirect control doubly fed induction generator. An integrated M5P machine learning algorithm to overcome the classic dynamic disadvantages of traditional controllers and to reduce the computational complexity, thereby improving the dynamics and robustness of the doubly fed induction generator while ensuring optimal operation of the wind turbine. Finally, the modeling and global control of the 2MW is achieved for the two operating modes hypo- and hyper-synchronous. The results obtained showed that they could have an optimal active power supplied to the electrical network regardless of the operating mode of the generator.

articleTitle: Design of the AC Filter for Two-Level Converter Operating in IT Grids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents the procedure of selecting the parameters of a grid filter with a common mode choke. The document is organized as a case study, where an example is a multi-converter system supplied from a 500 V three-phase IT grid. Due to the same topology of AC/DC and DC/AC component converters, it is possible to use the same filter for both converters. Particular attention is paid to the problems of the common mode choke, especially the issue of the core saturation effect. The proposed filter has been verified by laboratory tests.

articleTitle: Statistical Evaluation of Velocity Estimations from Temporal Fluoroscopic Angiography
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The vascular diseases are reflected by disorders in morphology and hemodynamics. For the diagnosis and treatment of these diseases, medical imagistic investigations are needed. They explore the morphological and functional aspects of blood circulation. The extraction of the blood flow from daily clinical acquisitions of X-ray angiography is of great importance for the physicians. The paper presents the implementation of bolus tracking algorithm which is related to contrast agent propagation into the blood stream for coronary vessels. The time density curve (TDC) is computed because it is a temporal evolution of the grey levels of a group of pixels tagged into an image set. For each image two TDCs are plotted into a dedicated MATLAB® based graphical user interface (GUI). The medical imagistic expert manually selects the proximal and the distal regions which delineates the vessel segment to be analyzed. The vessel length between the two regions is estimated enabling the velocity estimation. The image set is acquired from 20 patients, and it is investigated through 11 different transit time estimation methods. The results conduct to a future prototype system for diagnosis of vascular hemodynamic disorders.

articleTitle: Enhancing Home-Powered EV Fast-Charging Using a Hybrid Integrated Charger with Rooftop Solar and Local Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Aiming at the fast charging application for Electric Vehicles (EVs) using a residential local hybrid grid, this paper models a fast-charging network using the bidirectional three level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) DC-AC converter that is used as a traction inverter in EVs during propulsion mode. The proposed system models an AC-coupled local hybrid grid which includes local solar PV production, residential battery storage and local utility grid, that is capable of charging an EV battery at higher powers than otherwise provided by the On-Board Chargers (OBC). Utilizing the bidirectional NPC converter and the local hybrid grid will allow users to charge their EVs using the solar power generated during the day and stored in batteries more effectively.

articleTitle: Internet Based Control of a Servo Motor with a Sliding Mode Based Observer for Chattering Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This conference paper presents the sliding mode control of an Internet-based servo motor. The servo motor is equipped with an incremental encoder and the speed signal is obtained by digital derivation. Derivation is known to highlight noises. The state trajectory calculated from the noisy signal cannot remain on the sliding surface. Noise filtering introduces an unmodeled dynamics into the system. Due to this unmodeled dynamics, the state trajectory oscillates around the sliding surface. To reduce these oscillations, the article proposes an observer-based sliding mode controller. The article compares the classic and observer-based sliding mode controls by experimental measurement. The aim of the Internet-based servo motor to allow the students to reach the system, from their own computer via the internet, and to make the measurements from home. To do that they only need to know the basics of programming. With this servo system, the capacity of the measurement is increased. The students can use the system any time of the day.

articleTitle: Practical Challenges in Design of Omnidirectional, Medium Distance, Device Agnostic Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel omnidirectional wireless power transfer system is proposed. By having a centralized transmitter with an effective charging area where multiple receiver, can be placed limited by a distance of 10 cm. The transmitter utilizes a Class-E amplifier with a frequency of 6.78 MHz. In order to achieve omnidirectional flux with a limited power utilization, a switching matrix with edge-configurable coils has been proposed to achieve both horizontal and vertical flux. This paper deals with simulation, design and preliminary experimental testing of a Class-E amplifier based system with an output power of 15 W for device agnostic consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Overcurrent protection for auxiliary loads in Electric Vehicles with E-Fuse
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Some of the electric vehicle manufacturers intend to replace the thermal fuses used for auxiliary loads like AC compressor, DC-DC converter, heater, with electronic resettable fuses (E-Fuses). This paper presents an electronic fuse circuit designed according to the Automotive requirements. The circuit was designed considering tolerances and temperature dependent behavior of the components. Compared with the fast melting fuses, E-Fuses provide a very short disconnection time.

articleTitle: Fault detection in PMSM by using indexed based methods
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In general, permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) require four main sensors (two current sensors, one position sensor, and a dc-link voltage sensor) for continuous performance. If a sudden fault occurs in any one or more sensors, the performance of the drive deteriorates and the system becomes unstable. The existing works are limited to fault detection of a single sensor. To this end, we analyze the performance of several indices for single and multi-fault sensor fault detection scenarios. The suitability of these indices for PMSM is analyzed. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the pros and cons of various methods for fault detection.

articleTitle: Virtual Thermal Prototyping of the Power Module of the PCA-1 Drivetrain
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents the use of the virtual prototyping method associated with the thermal analysis of the power module, which is part of the suspended battery drivetrain type PCA-1. The main objective of the analysis was to evaluate the thermal effects associated with the battery operation, in connection with the planned increase in the load parameters. The indicated power module will be adapted to cooperate with the wireless power supply module, enabling charging also while the drivetrain is in motion.

articleTitle: Switched-Capacitor Boost Converter for Low Step-Up Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a new switched-capacitor step-up dc-dc converter which exhibits smooth output current and employs one active switch and four diodes. Compared to classical boost converter, at the same duty cycle, the proposed topology has a lower conversion ratio, thus being suitable for applications where a small step-up of the input voltage is required. The measured efficiency of about 90% over a wide duty cycle range is another feature of this new converter. As the topology belongs to the switched-capacitor family, for the first time the dc analysis is extended to the situation when unequal capacitor values are assumed. The main equations and the semiconductor stresses are evaluated. An experimental prototype of this new converter was first simulated and then practically tested and the results confirmed the theoretical considerations.

articleTitle: Design of an Individual Fingers Rehabilitation Device
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Hand rehabilitation robots will have a future due to the increase in stroke patients yearly. The aim of this project is to reduce the cost and the size of the robot to help as many patients as possible. This paper discussed new mechanism that can drive the motion for individual finger. The CAD model of the proposed Hand Rehabilitation Device (HRD) is works to transfer the angular velocity of the motor into prismatic motion that follow the natural movement of the finger. The derived motion of the model was capture with a motion capture software to track the desired trajectories.

articleTitle: A Novel Fourth-Order Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a novel fourth-order Buck-Boost converter with coupled inductors, one MOSFET transistor, three diodes, 2 capacitors and a separate inductor. The advantage of the proposed converter compared with the classical one is that it employs two degrees of freedom and for the same duty cycle provides a substantial higher output voltage. The dc and ac analyses are performed, and the design equations are provided. First, in order to test the functionality of the converter and to confirm the theoretical analysis, the fourth-order Buck-Boost converter is first subjected to simulation and then verified by practical experiments in open loop. In the last part, a state space model is provided for calculating the control to output transfer function. As the converter is of fourth order an approximation is used for reducing the control to output function order to two. The approximated transfer function has 99.34% approximation and contains a zero and two poles. Based on it a controller is designed and finally the theoretical considerations in closed loop operation are verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Manufacturing of IE4 induction motors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In the context of pessimistic climate change scenarios, the reduction of the electricity consumption is one of the key measures to be implemented. As electrical motors are one of the major energy consumers, the transition to higher efficiency classes is mandatory. Nowadays, the induction motor manufacturers (and not only) need to comply with more rigorous standards, such as IE4. This paper presents the efforts undertaken by S.C. Electroprecizia Electrical Motors SRL Săcele to bring the efficiency of the induction motors in the imposed interval. Information about the prototyping stages, the applied technical solutions and the obtained results in case of the 1.5kW 2 pole pairs motor is provided.

articleTitle: Applicability of 6/10 Switched Reluctance Motor as a Mid Drive e-Bike Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores the applicability of a 6/10 SRM for mid-drive bike propulsion as an efficient and cost-effective replacement for commonly used permanent magnet motors. Properties of the IPM Shimano Steps motor are explored first as this motor is used as a benchmark machine to compare the capabilities of the SRM. Based on the analyzed IPM, a set of requirements is defined for the design and optimization of 6/10 SRM. The optimal design of the SRM is compared with IPM in terms of torque and efficiency in the complete speed range. A prototype of the optimal design was built and compared with electromagnetic calculations for the sake of validation.

articleTitle: Impact of Discharge Current Profiles on Li-ion Battery Pack Degradation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Increasing the life cycle of battery packs is one of the most valuable endeavors in modern Li-ion battery technologies, especially for light electric vehicles whose material costs are often significantly determined by the costs of the battery pack.
